title: Build a Trust-Safe Citation Verifier
summary: Build a working, governed system that catches fabricated, mis-stated, and unsupported citations before they ship. Async course with a built-in AI tutor. No coding background needed.
audience: Researchers, writers, legal teams, educators, and publishers responsible for claims that must be traceable and correct.
learningPaths: Define the claim and citation contract
Test whether the source supports the claim
evidence: Primary sources and authoritative source records
Known-good and known-bad citation test cases
methodology: Define what the verifier must establish
Separate source existence from claim support
Return inspectable evidence for every finding
Require human review for ambiguous or consequential claims
assumptions: Learners can supply representative claims and citations
Final publication decisions remain with an accountable human
limitations: A verifier cannot guarantee that every source is complete or authoritative
Course content is educational and does not replace professional legal or editorial review

title: Build a Legislative and Regulatory Tracker
summary: Build a tool that monitors bills and rules across jurisdictions, scores relevance, and summarizes each change with a citation to the primary source.
audience: Legal, policy, compliance, advocacy, and regulated-industry teams that cannot afford to miss material changes.

Domain reviewers define materiality and relevance
limitations: No monitor guarantees immediate detection of every change
Summaries are informational and do not replace jurisdiction-specific legal advice
editorialIntro: In a weekend, build a working tool that monitors bills and rules across jurisdictions, scores what matters to your organization, and summarizes every change with a citation back to the primary source.
No coding background needed · Async, lifetime access · Built-in governed AI tutor

editorialSections.title: Regulation moves faster than any inbox can keep up with

blocks.text: Fifty states plus federal agencies are all moving at once. A bill you did not see gets introduced, amended, and enrolled while you are watching a different one. For a regulated operator, missing a single change can mean a blown compliance deadline, a lost lobbying window, or advice that is already out of date.

Manual tracking does not scale and news alerts summarize badly. What you need is a tool that watches the primary sources, scores relevance to your organization, and summarizes each change with a citation you can verify. Build it once and you stop guessing.

editorialSections.title: A tracker that reads the source, not the headline

blocks.text: By the end you have a working system that monitors the jurisdictions you care about and returns scored, summarized changes, each one linked to the primary text so nothing is taken on faith.
Across jurisdictions
Watches bills and rules in the states and agencies you track.
Relevance to your org
Rates each item against your organization's profile so noise drops away.
What actually changed
Plain-language summary of the change, its stage, and its likely effect.
The primary source
Every summary links back to the bill or rule text, verifiable and not paraphrased into thin air.
What matters, to whom
Routes high-relevance changes to the right person with a clear reason.
Human signs off
On doubt it defaults to flag for review. You stay accountable; the tool assists.

editorialSections.title: Nine modules, every one ships part of the real system

blocks.text: You do not watch and forget. You leave each module with a working piece of your tracker.

items: The problem and the standard. How legislation and rulemaking move, where the primary sources live, and what tracked really means. You write your relevance rubric.
Set up your workspace. Accounts, model access, project structure, with zero assumptions and nothing technical taken for granted.
Define your watch list. Build the profile of jurisdictions, topics, and keywords that tells the tool what to follow.
Monitor the sources. Build the intake that pulls bills and rules from the jurisdictions on your list and detects changes.
Summarize with citations, the core. Summarize each change grounded in the primary text, with a link back, and no summary the source cannot support.
Score relevance. Rate each item against your org profile and route the ones that matter to the right owner.
Governance layer. Guardrails, uncertainty handling, default-to-human, and an audit log of every item tracked.
Evaluate your tracker. Test against a known set of changes; measure what it caught and what it missed; tune the rubric.
Put it to work and package it. Run it on your real jurisdictions, and if you want, how to offer tracking as a service.
